newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares rise, expected to track sideways.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares rise, expected to track sideways.

text.p: Slovenia's blue-chip SBI index firmed 0.79 percent on Friday, but traders forecast it would track sideways in a market affected by low demand and the absence of many investors due to the holidays.
"I expect the index will keep between 1,520 and 1,600 points over the next 14 days," said Tomi Apollonio, an analyst of bank A Banka.
The SBI index edged 12.4 points higher to 1,576.89. This week the index rose 1.56 percent.

Traders said the index could grow significantly toward the end of August in expectation of fresh foreign investment in the autumn as the strong dollar is expected to lure new international investors to the market.
Overall 16 shares rose, two fell and two were flat while eight were untraded. Turnover jumped to 245.1 million tolars from 163.7 million.
Petrol trader Petrol was the most actively traded share, rising 2.71 percent to 25,030 tolars on volume of 5,848 shares for total turnover of 146.4 million tolars.
"If expectations of good business results prove to be right the share could jump to 30,000 tolars in the month following the half year announcement," Apollonio said.
Preferred shares of trading firm Kovinotehna were the top gainer, jumping 9.35 percent to 503 tolars on volume of only one share.
Construction company GPG led decliners, tumbling 3.23 percent to 6,000 tolars on volume of 210 shares.
Market participants said the poor liquidity of both shares was the reason for their tendency to fluctuate strongly.
